readings.title: Shimshon in Azzah
readings.subtitle: The Gates of the City
readings.text: [Judges 16:1] And Shimshon went to Azzah, and saw a harlot there, and went in to her. [2] It was told to the Azzites, saying, “Shimshon has come here!” And they went round about and lay in wait for him all night at the gate of the city, and were silent all night, saying, “Let us wait till the morning light, then we shall kill him.” [3] And Shimshon lay till midnight, and at midnight he rose up and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts, and pulled them up, bar and all, and put them on his shoulders, and took them to the top of the hill that faces Ḥebron.

readings.title: Shimshon and Delilah
readings.subtitle: The Secret of His Strength
readings.text: [Judges 16:4] And it came to be afterward that he loved <dn>את</dn> a woman in the Waḥal Sorĕq, whose name was Delilah. [5] And the princes of the Peleshetites came up to her and said to her, “Entice him, and see where his great strength lies, and by what we might overpower him and bind him to humble him. And let every one of us give you eleven hundred pieces of silver.” [6] And Delilah said to Shimshon, “Please explain to me where your great strength lies, and with what you might be bound to humble you.” [7] And Shimshon said to her, “If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings, not yet dried, then I shall be weak and be like any other man.” [8] And the princes of the Peleshetites brought up to her <dn>את</dn> seven fresh bowstrings, not yet dried, and she bound him with them. [9] Now men were lying in wait, staying with her in the room. And she said to him, “The Peleshetites are upon you, Shimshon!” But he broke <dn>את</dn> the bowstrings as a strand of yarn breaks when it touches fire. So the secret of his strength was not known. [10] And Delilah said to Shimshon, “See, you have mocked me and told me lies. Now, please explain to me with what you might be bound.” [11] And he said to her, “If they bind me securely with new ropes that have never been used, then I shall be weak and be like any other man.” [12] And Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and said to him, “The Peleshetites are upon you, Shimshon!” And men were lying in wait, staying in the room. But he broke them from his arms like a thread. [13] And Delilah said to Shimshon, “Up to now you have mocked me and told me lies. Explain to me with what you might be bound.” And he said to her, “If you weave <dn>את</dn> the seven locks of my head into the web of the loom.” [14] So she fastened it with the pin, and said to him, “The Peleshetites are upon you, Shimshon!” And he awoke from his sleep, and pulled out <dn>את</dn> the pin of the loom and <dn>את</dn> the web. [15] And she said to him, “How do you say, ‘I love you,’ when your heart is not with me? You have mocked me these three times, and have not explained to me where your great strength lies.” [16] And it came to be, when she pressed him daily with her words and urged him, so that his soul was impatient to death, [17] that he explained <dn>את</dn> all his heart to her, and said to her, “No razor has ever come upon my head, for I have been a Nazirite to <dn>Elohim</dn> from my mother’s womb. If I am shaven, then my strength shall leave me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.” [18] And when Delilah saw that he had explained <dn>את</dn> all his heart to her, she sent and called for the princes of the Peleshetites, saying, “Come up once more, for he has explained <dn>את</dn> all his heart to me.” And the princes of the Peleshetites came up to her and brought <dn>את</dn> the money in their hand. [19] And she lulled him to sleep on her knees, and called for a man and shaved off <dn>את</dn> the seven locks of his head. And she began to humble him, and his strength left him. [20] And she said, “The Peleshetites are upon you, Shimshon!” And he awoke from his sleep, and said, “Let me go out as at other times, and shake myself free!” But he did not know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had turned aside from him. [21] And the Peleshetites seized him and put out <dn>את</dn> his eyes, and brought him down to Azzah. And they bound him with bronze fetters, and he became a grinder in the prison house. [22] However, the hair of his head began to grow again after it had been shaven.

readings.title: The Death of Shimshon
readings.subtitle: Victory in Death
readings.text: [Judges 16:23] And the princes of the Peleshetites gathered to offer a great slaughter to Dagon their mighty one, and to rejoice. And they said, “Our mighty one has given <dn>את</dn> Shimshon our enemy into our hands!” [24] And when the people saw <dn>את</dn> him, they praised their mighty one, for they said, “Our mighty one has given <dn>את</dn> our enemy into our hands, and <dn>את</dn> the destroyer of our land, and <dn>את</dn> the one who multiplied our dead.” [25] And it came to be, when their hearts were glad, that they said, “Call for Shimshon, and let him perform for us.” So they called for Shimshon from the prison house, and he performed for them. And they stationed him between the columns. [26] And Shimshon said to the young man who held him by the hand, “Let me alone, and let me feel <dn>את</dn> the columns which support the house, so that I lean on them.” [27] Now the house was full of men and women. And all the princes of the Peleshetites were there. And about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching while Shimshon performed. [28] And Shimshon cried to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, remember me, I pray! Strengthen me, I pray, only this time, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, and let me take vengeance on the Peleshetites for <dn>את</dn> my two eyes!” [29] And Shimshon took hold of <dn>את</dn> the two middle columns which supported the house, and he braced himself against them, one on his right and the other on his left. [30] And Shimshon said, “Let me die with the Peleshetites!” And he bowed himself with might, and the house fell on the princes and all the people who were in it. So the dead <dn>את</dn> that he killed at his death were more than he had killed in his life. [31] And his brothers and all his father’s household came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Tsor‛ah and Eshta’ol in the burial-place of Manoḥ his father. And he judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl twenty years.

readings.title: Miḵah's Idolatry
readings.subtitle: A Levite for Hire
readings.text: [Judges 17:1] And there was a man from the mountains of Ephrayim, whose name was Miḵah. [2] And he said to his mother, “The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you, and on which you put a curse, even saying it in my ears, see, the silver is with me; I took it.” And his mother said, “Blessed be my son by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!” [3] So he returned <dn>את</dn> the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother. And his mother said, “I had set <dn>את</dn> the silver apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for my son, to make a carved image and a moulded image. And now, I return it to you.” [4] But he returned <dn>את</dn> the silver to his mother, and his mother took <dn>את</dn> two hundred pieces of silver and gave them to the silversmith, and he made it into a carved image and a moulded image. And they were in the house of Miḵah. [5] And the man Miḵah had a shrine, and made an ephod and household idols. And he ordained <dn>את</dn> one of his sons, and he became his priest. [6] In those days there was no sovereign in Yisra’ĕl, everyone did what was right in his own eyes. [7] And there was a young man from Bĕyth Leḥem in Yehudah, of the clan of Yehudah. And he was a Lĕwite, and was sojourning there. [8] And the man went from the city of Bĕyth Leḥem in Yehudah to sojourn where he could find a place. And he came to the mountains of Ephrayim, to the house of Miḵah, as he journeyed. [9] And Miḵah said to him, “Where do you come from?” And he said to him, “I am a Lĕwite from Bĕyth Leḥem in Yehudah, and I am on my way to find a place to sojourn.” [10] And Miḵah said to him, “Dwell with me, and be a father and a priest to me, and I give you ten pieces of silver a year, and a suit of garments, and your food.” So the Lĕwite went in. [11] And the Lĕwite agreed to dwell with <dn>את</dn> the man. And the young man was like one of his sons to him. [12] And Miḵah ordained <dn>את</dn> the Lĕwite, and the young man became his priest, and lived in the house of Miḵah. [13] And Miḵah said, “Now I know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does good to me, since I have a Lĕwite as priest!”

readings.title: The Tribe of Dan Seeks Territory
readings.subtitle: The Theft of Miḵah's Idols
readings.text: [Judges 18:1] In those days there was no sovereign in Yisra’ĕl. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking an inheritance for itself to dwell in, for until that day an inheritance among the tribes of Yisra’ĕl had not fallen to them. [2] And the children of Dan sent five men of their clan from their borders, men of valour from Tsor‛ah and from Eshta’ol, to spy out <dn>את</dn> the land and search <dn>את</dn> it. And they said to them, “Go, search <dn>את</dn> the land.” And they came to the mountains of Ephrayim, to the house of Miḵah, and spent the night there. [3] While they were at the house of Miḵah, they recognised <dn>את</dn> the voice of the young Lĕwite. And they turned aside there and said to him, “Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this place? And what do you have here?” [4] And he said to them, “Thus and thus Miḵah did for me, and hired me, and I became his priest.” [5] And they said to him, “Please inquire of <dn>Elohim</dn>, that we might know whether the way on which we go is prosperous.” [6] And the priest said to them, “Go in peace. The presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with the way you go.” [7] And the five men went and came to Layish, and saw <dn>את</dn> the people who were there, how they dwelt safely, according to the ruling of the Tsidonians, quiet and unsuspecting. And there was no ruler in the land to humiliate them in any matter. And they were far from the Tsidonians, and they had no word with any man. [8] And they came back to their brothers at Tsor‛ah and Eshta’ol, and their brothers said to them, “What do you say?” [9] And they said, “Arise, and let us go up against them. For we have seen <dn>את</dn> the land, and see, it is very good. And you, are you keeping silent? Do not hesitate to go, to enter to possess <dn>את</dn> the land. [10] “When you go, you come to an unsuspecting people, and the land is large. For <dn>Elohim</dn> has given it into your hands, a place where there is no lack of any matter that is on the earth.” [11] And six hundred men of the clan of the Danites went from there, from Tsor‛ah and from Eshta’ol, girded with weapons of battle. [12] And they went up and encamped in Qiryath Ye‛arim in Yehudah. Therefore they call that place Maḥaneh Dan to this day. See, it is west of Qiryath Ye‛arim. [13] And they passed over from there to the mountains of Ephrayim, and came to the house of Miḵah. [14] And the five men who had gone to spy out <dn>את</dn> the country of Layish answered and said to their brothers, “Do you know that there are in these houses an ephod, and household idols, and a carved image, and a moulded image? And now, know what you should do.” [15] And they turned aside there and came to the house of the young Lĕwite, to the house of Miḵah, and asked him of his welfare. [16] And the six hundred men girded with their weapons of battle, who were of the children of Dan, stood by the entrance of the gate. [17] And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up, came in there, and took <dn>את</dn> the carved image, <dn>את</dn> the ephod, and <dn>את</dn> the household idols, and <dn>את</dn> the moulded image. And the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men who were girded with weapons of battle. [18] And when these went into Miḵah’s house and took <dn>את</dn> the carved image, the ephod, and <dn>את</dn> the household idols, and <dn>את</dn> the moulded image, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?” [19] And they said to him, “Be silent, put your hand over your mouth, and come with us, and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest to the household of one man, or that you be a priest to a tribe and a clan in Yisra’ĕl?” [20] And the priest’s heart was glad. And he took <dn>את</dn> the ephod, and <dn>את</dn> the household idols, and <dn>את</dn> the carved image, and took his place among the people. [21] And they turned and went away, and put <dn>את</dn> the little ones, and <dn>את</dn> the livestock, and <dn>את</dn> the valuables in front of them. [22] They had gone far from the house of Miḵah, when the men who were in the houses near Miḵah’s house gathered together and overtook <dn>את</dn> the children of Dan. [23] And they called out to the children of Dan. And they turned their faces and said to Miḵah, “What is the matter with you, that you have gathered together?” [24] And he said, “You have taken away <dn>את</dn> my mighty ones which I made, and <dn>את</dn> the priest, and you have gone away. Now what more do I have? How then do you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’ ” [25] And the children of Dan said to him, “Do not let your voice be heard among us, lest men bitter of soul fall upon you, and you lose your life, with the lives of your household!” [26] And the children of Dan went their way. And Miḵah saw that they were too strong for him, so he turned and went back to his house. [27] And they took <dn>את</dn> what Miḵah had made, and <dn>את</dn> the priest who had belonged to him, and went to Layish, to a people quiet and unsuspecting. And they smote them with the edge of the sword and burned <dn>את</dn> the city with fire. [28] And there was no deliverer, because it was far from Tsidon, and they had no word with any man. And it was in the valley that belongs to Bĕyth Reḥob. And they built the city and dwelt in it. [29] And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Yisra’ĕl. However, the name of the city was formerly Layish. [30] And the children of Dan set up <dn>את</dn> the carved image for themselves. And Yehonathan the son of Gĕrshom, the son of Menashsheh, and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land. [31] So they set up for themselves <dn>את</dn> Miḵah’s carved image which he made, all the days that the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> was in Shiloh.
